title: Gradient direction and feature scale
prompt: For squared-error linear regression with prediction `Xw`, explain what the gradient with respect to `w` measures, why moving against it reduces loss for a sufficiently small step, and why features on very different scales can make gradient descent inefficient. Include the gradient shape.
expected_concepts: Residuals are mapped back through the transposed design matrix
The gradient has one component per model weight
The negative gradient is the local steepest-descent direction
Feature scaling improves conditioning and step-size behavior

rubric.criterion: Relates the gradient to residuals and X transpose
Explains the local descent direction and step-size condition
Connects feature scale to optimization conditioning

hints: Differentiate the residual square, then apply the chain rule through `Xw`.
Visualize elongated loss contours for unequal feature scales.
follow_ups: How does adding L2 regularization change the gradient?
Why does scaling not fix perfect collinearity?
